DATED:
 
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CIVIL APPLICATION (FOR CONDONATION OF DELAY) NO. 4449 of  2024  In F/FIRST APPEAL NO. 23571 of 2024  ================================================================
 THE DEPUTY ENGINEER, WESTERN RAILWAYS  Versus  AMRUBHAI VAJSURBHAI & ORS.
 ================================================================
 Appearance:
 MS ARCHANA U AMIN(2462) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR ADITYA D DAVDA, AGP for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR DHAIRYAWAN D BHATT(11817) for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ================================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 13/09/2024

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.
This application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 1220 days in preferring the appeal.
2. Heard learned advocate Mr. Archana U. Amin for the applicant.

Learned advocate Mr.
Dhairyawan D. Bhatt for the respondent No.1 and learned Assistant Government Pleader Mr. Aditya D. Davda for the respondent No.2.

3. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that learned Principal Senior Civil Judge,
Gandhinagar passed a NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined judgment and award dated 20.12.2018 in Land Reference Case No.518 of 2017 enhancing the compensation at Rs.700/- per sq. Mtr. for the irrigated land and Rs.500/- per sq. Mtr. for non- irrigated land.

It is further submitted that impugned judgment of the learned Reference Court was challenged by the opponent No.2-State by way of F/First Appeal No.11067 of 2021, however, for non-removal of office objections, the appeal came to be dismissed on 15.07.2022.

The said appeal The Deputy Engineer, Western Railways vs Amrubhai Vajsurbhai on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8086714/
1 has not been restored at the instance of State.

sentences.text: Opponent No.1-original claimant filed execution petition seeking execution of the judgment and award.

The original claimant also preferred Special Civil Application being No.8374 of 2024 before this Court seeking direction to expedite the proceedings of the execution, which came to be allowed on 29.07.2024.

entities.text: Special Civil Application being No.8374 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Thereafter, pursuant to the order passed by the Executing Court, the present applicant deposited the amount of compensation in the execution proceedings.

It is further submitted that the opponent No.2-State as well as the applicants have filed First Appeal NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined arising out of the cognate groups of the same village, which are admitted by this Court.
The acquisition was for the same purpose.

It is further submitted certified copy of the impugned judgment and award was applied on 15.07.2024 which was received on 16.07.2024 and thereafter, the appeal is filed with an application for condonation of delay.
It is further submitted that there is no negligence and intentional delay on the part of the applicant in challenging the impugned judgment and award.
It is further submitted that if the delay is not condoned, it would have a great effect on other appeals, which would be filed within a very short period of time.
The said appeals would be arising from the same group, out of which, and one of the Land Reference Cases is of the same group.
It is further submitted that this Court may take a lenient view looking to the facts and circumstances of the present case and condone delay.

4. Per contra, learned advocate for the respondent No.1 has vehemently objected in granting of the application and has NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined relied upon the contentions raised in the affidavit-in-reply dated 10.09.2024.

It is further submitted that learned Reference Court passed an order on 20.12.2018 in Land Reference Case No.518 of 2017, which is forming part of the group of Land Reference Cases Nos.483/2017 to 494/2017, Land Reference Cases Nos.496/2017 to 501/2017, Land Reference Cases Nos.507/2017 to 509/2017, Land Reference Case No.511/2017, Land Reference Case No518/2017 and Land Reference Case No519/2017.
It is further submitted that since the award was not satisfied, the claimants filed execution petition being Execution Application No.24 of 2021.
Pursuant to a notice dated 19.03.2021, issued by the learned Executing Court, the present applicants appeared in the proceedings.
An application for issuance of warrant for attachment of properties also came to be filed by the claimants on 04.03.2023 in the execution proceedings.

It is further submitted that State filed First Appeal challenging impugned judgment and award, however, the said appeal came to be dismissed for non-removal of office NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined objections on 15.07.2022
. Pursuant to the order passed by the learned Execution Court, applicant deposited the amount of compensation.
It is submitted that after passing of the order in Special Civil Application No.8374 of 2024 on 29.07.2024, the applicant filed the present appeal with a prayer for condonation of delay.
It is further submitted that there is a gross delay of 1220 days in filing the appeal.
It is further submitted that the application is vague and does not disclose any sufficient cause.
It is further submitted by the learned advocate for the opponent No.1 that in view of the decision in the case of Pathapati Subba Reddy (Died) By L.Rs. & Ors. Vs.

sentences.text: The Special Deputy Collector (LA) reported in 2024 0 Supreme(SC) 322, in which, while discussing on the law of limitation, Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down guidelines.
It is held by Hon'ble Apex Court that appeals preferred after expiry of limitation are liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: It is further pointed out that in the present case, the applicant has remained idle and was not vigilant about the right NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined to challenge the judgment and award.
In view of these facts, learned advocate for the opponent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of the present application.
5. I have heard the submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties and also perused the affidavit-in-reply filed by the opponent No.1.
The applicant herein has assailed the judgment and order dated 20.12.2018 passed in Land Reference Case.
After the decision of the learned trial Court, the applicant neither comply with the order nor filed any appeal.
The opponent No.2-State filed an appeal being F/First Appeal No.11067 of 2021 which came to be dismissed for non-removal of office objection on 15.07.2022.
The said appeal till today has not been restored to its original file.
When opponent No.1 filed execution petition, the applicant appeared in the year 2021.
Even thereafter the applicant did not challenge the judgment and order.

The claimant was constrained to file Special Civil Application being No.8374 of 2024 seeking NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined direction from this Court to expedite the execution proceedings.

entities.text: Special Civil Application being No.8374 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Upon passing the order by this Court, the learned Executing Court directed the applicant to deposit the amount of compensation which was ultimately deposited by the applicant in execution proceedings.

6. Learned advocate for the applicant has mainly harped upon the fact that the State as well as the applicant has filed First Appeals which are arising out of the cognate group of Land Acquisition Reference Cases pertaining to the same village and pertaining to the same purpose of acquisition.

The only contention which has been raised by the learned advocate for the applicant is that if the delay is not condoned, it would have an adverse effect on those appeals, which are already pending for its adjudication.

Another submission made by the learned advocate for the applicant is that the judgment and order of the learned Land Reference Court and other Land Reference Cases are also under the process of challenge by the applicant.
These NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined contentions are hollow contentions and does not inspire this Court to take a lenient approach.

The applicant was aware about the execution proceedings in the year 2021, there is no explanation in the application as to why the applicant did not challenge the impugned judgment and award at the relevant point of time.

Even on perusal of the application,
no such explanation is forthcoming for the period after 2021 till the order passed in Special Civil Application No.8374 of 2024.
The only explanation which is canvassed by the applicant is that the State filed an appeal which came to be dismissed on 15.07.2022.
There is no explanation for the period after 15.07.2022 till filing of present application.
When the applicant remained idle and did not remain vigilant about the challenge against the impugned judgment and order, no leniency can be expected from the Court.
Court would exercise its discretionary power by taking a lenient view for the litigants who have remained vigilant and active with regard to their rights.

By non-condoning delay, adverse effect would be on the other First Appeals, which are NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined pending out of cognate group of matters,
is not a sufficient cause for condoning delay.
This Court has also considered the fact that the present Appeal is filed only against the decision rendered in Land Reference Case No.518 of 2017.
And for other group of Land Reference Cases, as per the submission of learned advocate for the applicant, no appeals are filed till today.

It seems that the applicant has taken a chance by filing only one appeal The Deputy Engineer, Western Railways vs Amrubhai Vajsurbhai on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8086714/
3 with a request for condonation of delay and waited for the outcome of the present application.

entities.text: Deputy Engineer, Western Railways vs Amrubhai Vajsurbhai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The conduct of applicant in not challenging judgment and award and other reference cases is really surprising.
7. In the decision of Pathapati Subba Reddy (supra), in paragraph Nos.7, 8, 12, 16 and 26, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down the law and has discussed what is "sufficient cause".

In clause No.(vi) of para 26, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that merely some persons obtained relief in other similar matters, it does not mean that others are also entitled to NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the same benefit, if the Court is not satisfied with the cause shown for the delay in filing the appeal.
Adopting this observation, in the present case, no sufficient cause is made out by the applicant.
The reasons which are mentioned in the application are by no stretch of imagination be construed as sufficient cause.
On the contrary, it gives a clear picture that applicant being a Government Organization has remained absolutely careless and negligent and in not challenging the decision within a reasonable time.
When the State failed in assailing the judgment and order, all of a sudden, the applicant came out of the slumber and challenged the judgment and order dated 20.12.2018.
Certified copy of the impugned judgment and award was applied after expiry of limitation period for filing appeal.
Such is not a bonafide conduct of applicant.

Application for obtaining certified copy of judgment and order after the prescribed period of limitation, for filing Appeal / Application disentitles the applicant in challenging judgment and award, unless a very sound and convincing explanation is pleaded and NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/4449/2024 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined shown by applicant in not applying certified copy of judgment and award within the prescribed period of limitation.
Thus, in my view, no sufficient cause is made out in the application which tempts this Court to adopt a lenient approach in favour of applicant.
Resultantly, the application stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(D. M. DESAI,J) RINKU MALI The Deputy Engineer, Western Railways vs Amrubhai Vajsurbhai on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8086714/
